Cross-section layout with automatic deconfliction

Source: R/cross_section_layout.R
cross_section_layout.Rd

Build reviewable channel and overbank XS segments from reviewed inundation footprints, with polygon-derived direction, ordered endpoints and automatic deconfliction. Return source evidence and diagnostics for local draft workflows.

cross_section_layout(
  flowline,
  channel,
  floodplain,
  spacing_m = 20,
  tangent_distance_m = 20,
  angle_limit_deg = 30,
  centerline_spacing_m = 2,
  smoothing_refinements = 2L,
  region_artifacts = NULL,
  overbank_angle_limit_deg = 30,
  allow_overbank_bends = TRUE
)

Arguments

flowline

One simple LINESTRING, directed downstream to upstream.

channel, floodplain

Hole-filled sf polygon footprints in the same projected CRS as flowline. Channel must be contained in floodplain.

spacing_m

Distance between section centers in metres. Centers begin at half this distance from the downstream endpoint; endpoints are excluded.

tangent_distance_m

Distance along a polygon centerline for measuring its local tangent, in metres; independent of cartographic smoothing.

angle_limit_deg

Maximum channel-normal departure searched to resolve channel contacts, with or without overbanks, 0 to 60 degrees; default 30. Search uses 2.5-degree steps. Zero disables angular repair. Rotations above 15 degrees retain a review flag; these are provisional geometric settings, not hydraulic limits.

centerline_spacing_m

Maximum polygon-boundary vertex spacing in metres.

smoothing_refinements

Number of Chaikin smoothing passes, 0 to 10.

region_artifacts

Optional matching output of cross_section_regions(), reused only when its geometry/settings fingerprint matches these inputs. Its explicit prepare_channel choice is honored and recorded in parameters.

overbank_angle_limit_deg

Maximum overbank-normal rotation in degrees, 0 to 60. Straight targets respect this bound; five-degree angular alternatives provide tentative targets before ordered assignment and routing.

allow_overbank_bends

Allow additional floodplain vertices for deconfliction. Defaults to TRUE. Polygon-contained routes may have multiple vertices away from the centerline; there is no one-bend cap.

Value

A list with sections (sf lines with at least two XY vertices), paths (separate side estimates), samples (observed/inferred side evidence), failures, conflicts and parameters. Empty or unsupported sections remain explicit failures. candidate_id is a session key, not governed or durable identity. Full-coverage straight/bent alternatives reduce conflicts without shortening legs. Explicit left_bank_vertex and right_bank_vertex identify the channel. Residual conflicts remain explicit. Seq increases upstream. boundary_chains and boundary_anchors retain directed ordering edges and generated bank/planned outer targets in the feature CRS unit. Source/prepared channel polygons, the raw channel reference centerline and lobe review polygons retain channel-cleanup evidence. Per-side geodesic and group-routing flags distinguish generated evidence. channel_oriented checks channel-bank direction, outer_chord_oriented checks the endpoint chord, and the established oriented field retains their conjunction.

Details

Contiguous channel crossings containing each center are selected perpendicular to the local centerline tangent. Contacting channel windows may use bounded joint rotations before overbank construction. There is no width or length objective. All three polygon centerlines derive from Voronoi skeleton routing and cartographic Chaikin smoothing. An overbank leg uses the component touching its bank vertex. Missing/ambiguous side support retains a flagged bank-only leg. A bank on the outer boundary with no adjacent overbank is separately classified as no_floodplain. Method v7 omits absent or unconstructed overbank edges: channel-only cross sections have two vertices; a straight one-sided cross section has three. Failed construction retains its warning status and boundary gap. Explicit bank indices may identify endpoints; no zero-width placeholder edge is required. If nearest-point matching crosses a channel indentation, the nearest tested segment projection visible through the component supplies the measurement location. The original centerline is unchanged. A one-millimetre numerical polygon margin is used for visibility and connected ray intersections. Channel angular search includes up to two eligible neighbors on each side, at most 64 sections and 50,000 constraint-search nodes per window. A failed or exhausted search retains the original flagged geometry. Both bank rank and all-pair nonintersection must pass an independent final geometry audit. Bank ranks are checked along directed shared boundaries; outer targets are assigned in Seq order and refined within their ordered neighbor interval before routing. Previously accepted legs and other channel XS segments are barriers. A routed endpoint cannot slide along the boundary. These are provisional direction proxies requiring analyst review. All distance parameters are converted to the projected CRS unit. When additional vertices are allowed, GEOS constrained polygon triangulation, igraph paths through triangle portals and visibility shortcuts supply additional routes around neighboring sections. Bends need not be on a centerline. Every route must remain in its component and reach the outer boundary. This optional routing requires GEOS 3.10 or later. The channel polygon's own medial route and local width guide lobe cleanup before LOB/ROB partitioning. Hidden centerlines use contained mesh geodesic associations. Difficult overbank neighborhoods can be reconsidered together with fixed banks/targets; complete coverage precedes reducing interior crowding. Four priorities, 64-section groups and 16 exact-route fallbacks bound this search. Neither channel width nor section length is minimized. A subsequent whole-bend pass jointly tests targets and routes in families of at most 32 sections, including complete but crowded or awkward legs. It tests adaptive isotonic, relaxed and uniform target distributions in three routing orders, reusing valid existing paths as deformation guides before mesh reconstruction. Complete coverage, useful endpoint separation and fewer unnecessary turns take priority in that order. A complete incumbent is retained whenever no feasible improvement is found. Channel banks and saved Flowline stations remain fixed. Accepted method-v10 channel pruning is unchanged.
